current.text: Experts see him as fair value in the 20s for category leagues, around the end of round two or the start of round three. One expert says pick 11 on ESPN is far too high.
In a 2026-10-05 auction mock draft he went for 29 USD.
In that mock, Josh stopped bidding at 24 USD and did not see 29 USD as a bargain.
His free throw percentage and three-point shooting dropped last season. Experts disagree on a rebound: one says his shooting could bounce back, another says it is unclear.
He is projected to start at guard for Chicago. Nikola Vucevic and Coby White are gone, and Norman Powell has arrived.
His usage should drop because the Chicago roster is healthy. Norman Powell may lead the team in usage unless he is traded.
Experts project about 23 usage and 33 to 34 minutes.
He should be the offensive hub and reach about 10 assists per game. He still needs to score around 15 to 16 points because the team lacks shooting.
He dealt with ankle injuries last season.
He is the only Bulls player paid over 20 million USD per year, so he faces the most pressure if the season goes badly.
Chicago has a new head coach, Tiago Splitter, who replaces Billy Donovan.
Chicago is expected to be a bad team, probably bottom six, at about 32 wins. It should play fast and up-tempo, with poor spacing.
Chicago has 10 games in our fantasy playoff weeks (3-3-4) and 15 back-to-backs this season. It also has one of the season's three five-game weeks. The first 20 games are a hard stretch.

durable.text: He is reliable in points, rebounds and assists, with very high assists and rebounds for a guard. Rebounding and transition play are strengths.
He is not a high-usage player. His weekly variance comes from his percentages and steals.
He commits many turnovers, a clear weakness in the TO category.
He made about 37% and 36.5% of his threes over the last two seasons, on low volume.
He is worth more in points leagues than in 9-cat leagues.
Availability is a concern. He needs to play more than 60 to 65 games.

note: Experts value him as a pick in the 20s for category leagues. That is close to the 31 USD he cost in our league last season and the 29 USD from a recent mock auction, not his Yahoo value of 37 USD or his average cost of 34.6 to 37.4 USD. His assists (9.3 projected) and rebounds for a guard make him a top asset. His 3.6 turnovers hurt, so he fits a punt TO build best and fits weakly where turnovers matter. Early in the season, watch whether his FT% gets back near 78%, how much usage he shares with Norman Powell, whether his assists reach about 10, and whether he stays healthy after last season's 54 games.
